_comment: CONFORMANCE VECTOR for spec §4e's key-less cap: a policy holds AT MOST ONE
key-less spend path. Composer fable review r0, lens 1, C-1.
WHY IT EXISTS. Paths chain right-leaning as or_i(P, rest) (or_d under a
bare-multi head), and or_i(l, r) is non-malleable only if l.safe || r.safe
-- `safe` meaning every satisfaction needs a signature. A key-less path is
never safe, so two of them ANYWHERE in the list leave some or_i on the
spine with two unsafe arms: `md encode` refuses the template as malleable
and Bitcoin Core refuses the import (`not sane: malleable witnesses
exist`), keyed path included. A TIMELOCK DOES NOT HELP -- older/after need
no signature either.
The Rust primary used to reach that verdict only by re-parsing its own
output in `md compose` (md-cli F-600). The device's Go port has no
rust-miniscript and cannot read back, so it cut such a policy into steel.
The rule now lives in md_codec::compose::validate(), which md/compose.go
ports -- and this file is what the port conforms to.
HAND-WRITTEN, NOT GENERATED. `md vectors` exports ADMITTED policies (a
template, a card, addresses); a refusal has none of those, so this vector
is maintained by hand and excluded from the corpus-drift diff in
md-cli/tests/vector_corpus.rs. Its Rust gate is
md-codec/tests/compose_keyless_cap.rs.
MEASUREMENT behind `refused_when`: 859 wsh path lists of 2 to 4 paths over
five keyed and four key-less atoms, driven through `md compose
--wrapper wsh --experimental` at md-cli 0.16.2. All 504 lists with two or
more key-less paths were refused after lowering; all 355 with at most one
were emitted. Zero counterexamples.
rule: a policy holds at most one key-less spend path
refused_when: two or more paths are key-less -- `keys == null` AND `hash != null` (a path with neither keys nor hash is LockOnlyPath, refused earlier) -- at any positions, whatever locks they carry

error_fields.first: 0-based index of the first key-less path
error_fields.second: 0-based index of the second key-less path

precedence: KeylessUnderTr comes first under wrapper tr (the tr rule is the one in force there)
NoKeyedPath comes first when no path has a key at all (BIP-388 l.191)
TooManySlots comes first when the slot total exceeds 32 (folding two key-less paths into one does not shed a slot)
LegacyWrapperShape comes first under sh / sh-wsh (folding leaves two paths, still not one sorted multisig)
Every precedence rule has a case below; a port that orders the cap ahead of any of them still refuses, but names a remedy that does not work

cases.name: keyed_then_two_keyless
cases.message: paths 2 and 3 both have no key; side by side they lower to a malleable `or_i` that `md encode` refuses and no wallet will import. Give one of them a key, a timelock does not help, or fold them into one path

cases.name: keyed_then_two_keyless_second_locked
cases.message: paths 2 and 3 both have no key; side by side they lower to a malleable `or_i` that `md encode` refuses and no wallet will import. Give one of them a key, a timelock does not help, or fold them into one path

cases.name: two_keyless_split_by_a_keyed_path
cases.message: paths 1 and 3 both have no key; side by side they lower to a malleable `or_i` that `md encode` refuses and no wallet will import. Give one of them a key, a timelock does not help, or fold them into one path

cases.name: one_locked_keyless_head_then_multi
cases._control: ADMITTED. A port that refused every key-less path would satisfy the three cases above and delete the EXPERIMENTAL feature.
